before.paraphrase: The child asks the gods not to drive him away by force when they see the demon, but to watch his and the demon’s remarkable encounter. They joyfully yet uncertainly discuss his capacity and bow. Analāsura approaches as dissolution-fire, burning ten directions and devouring humans. The people cry out and sages flee, warning the child to escape before the fire kills him, comparing it with a great predator. Gaṇeśa stands firm like Himavat; they retreat far away, leaving him there.
before.verification_notes: Direct Sanskrit body reading; not independent edition verification. Uncertain Sanskrit clauses identified separately.

findings.description: Printed nodanīyo balād aham is a positive passive instruction, to be impelled/urged forcibly by all of you on seeing the demon. Draft introduces an unsupported negative. MW nud supports push/impel/urge senses. Do not supply an unstated push direction or claim gods actually carry out the instruction; their later retreat and deity’s māyā capture remain distinct.

after.paraphrase: The child announces a means of killing the demon and directs the gods to carry it out.
